input.quote: (a) Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees from all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees) or liabilities ("Claims") arising out of or in connection with:
input.rationale: Section 10(a) contains a broad Vendor (Kubient) defence and indemnity in our favour covering third-party Claims arising out of or in connection with the Services, the Auction Platform, Creative placed on our properties, Vendor's breach of its representations and warranties, and the acts or omissions of Vendor and its subcontractors. Because it is triggered by any third-party claim connected with the Services or Platform, it captures third-party IP infringement/misappropriation allegations and Vendor misconduct, and it is not limited by the usual exclusions or a super-cap — indeed the indemnity is expressly carved out of the consequential-damages exclusion in Section 7(a), so it sits at or above the preferred position. Section 11 supplies the standard procedure (prompt notice with no forfeiture for delay, indemnifying-party control, no liability-admitting settlement without consent, cooperation at the indemnifying party's cost). Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording but are not material deviations: our reciprocal indemnity in Section 10(b) is broader than "Customer content and Customer's breach of law" (it also reaches unauthorised use, breach of warranty and Customer acts/omissions), and Vendor's indemnity for Creative is qualified by "to the best of its knowledge." Both are noted for negotiation leverage rather than redlined, since the Vendor-side obligation — the subject of this rule — is fully satisfied and the structure is mutual.
